articles.dek: For decades, Korea’s unique “jeonse” rental system was widely seen as a natural stepping stone to homeownership. Under jeonse, tenants pay their landlord a large lump-sum deposit — often equivalent to 60 to 80 percent of the property’s value — instead of monthly rent. The deposit is returned in full when the lease ends, typically after two years.
